Answer: B
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates dense, curvilinear calcification outlining the anterior and inferior borders of the heart, specifically following the contour of the right ventricle and atrioventricular groove. This "eggshell" calcification pattern is pathognomonic for constrictive calcified pericarditis, which can present with signs of right heart failure and murmurs due to altered hemodynamics.
